4. A reply to a reply is counted in the issue's comment count but does not appear in the thread.
5. When a comment is deleted, the replies beneath it disappear as well.
6. Editing a comment to add a mention does not alert the newly mentioned person, the comment keeps listing the old mentions, and searching for the new wording does not find it.
7. The fifteen-minute edit limit only holds for comments that were never edited: people who edit once within the window keep editing for days.
8. Nobody is told when someone replies to their comment.

Anyone who is currently an active member of the workspace can be mentioned by their handle — the part of their email address before the @, matched case-insensitively — whatever their role and however many members the workspace has. A handle shared by several members mentions all of them. The members recorded as mentioned on a comment, and alerted, are exactly those its text mentions (outside code), except the comment's author, whose own handle is ignored. Members of other workspaces are never mentioned, whatever their handle.

When a comment is posted, the issue's author, its current assignee and — for a reply — the author of the comment being answered are told that a comment was added, and the people the comment mentions are told that they were mentioned. Each person gets at most one alert for one comment, and a mention alert takes precedence over a comment alert. The comment's author gets nothing. Each recipient's notification preferences apply as for any other alert.

  - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions 
- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it
- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit
- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries
- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive

  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.).   - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose

   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

- NEVER use the TaskCreate or Agent tools

- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.

   - Use the description/body for details, not the title

## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

- DO NOT use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )

## 1. @-mentions parsing

**`src/lib/mentions.ts`** — server/shared authority on what a comment body *means*.
- `MENTION_PATTERN` (line 14): `/(^|[\s(<[])@([a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,38}[a-z0-9])/gi` — requires `@` to start the string or follow whitespace/`(`/`<`/`[`, so an email's `@` is never matched.
- `handleOf(member)` (21-23): handle = `member.user.email.split("@")[0]`, lowercased.
- `extractMentions(body)` (26-38): strips fenced/backtick code first via `withoutCode` (16-18), returns distinct lowercased handles in first-appearance order.
- `resolveMentions(body, members)` (45-67): builds `handle → userId` map, **skipping `role === "viewer"` members** (line 53, "Read-only members cannot take part in a discussion, so pinging them only produces an alert they can do nothing about") — this is a deliberate business rule to note for any mention-related bug fix. Unknown handles are silently dropped. De-dupes resolved ids.
- `highlightMentions(body)` (70-76): wraps matches in `<span class="mention">`.

**`src/components/domain/comment/mention-query.ts`** — client-side "caret" half (autocomplete UX), intentionally kept separate from the parsing authority above:
- `findMentionQuery(body, caret)` (29-44): locates the in-progress `@token` at the caret.
- `mentionHandle(member)` (47-50): **duplicate/independent implementation** of the handle derivation (falls back to `member.user.name` if no local part, where `mentions.ts`'s `handleOf` falls back to `""`). Two sources of truth for "what is a handle" — worth checking they can't diverge on edge cases (e.g. empty local part).
- `matchMembers` (53-68), `applyMention` (71-79) for autocomplete UI.

**`src/components/domain/comment/mention-textarea.tsx`** — calls `resolveMentions` from `@/lib/mentions` directly (line 8, 37) so client-reported mentions match server parsing.

**Mention resolution in the write path** — `src/server/services/comment-service.ts`, `resolveMentionedUsers()` (176-193): fetches up to `MENTION_LOOKUP_LIMIT = 100` members (line 34) via `memberRepo.listMembers`, calls `resolveMentions(body, members.items)`, then unions with client-provided `mentionedUserIds` **filtered to known member ids** — "The server list wins on disagreement" (comment at 172-175). Note: only the first 100 members are scanned for mention resolution, which could silently drop mentions in larger orgs.

**Tests**: `tests/lib/mentions.test.ts` (extraction order/case-insensitivity/code-span exclusion/email exclusion/dedup/unknown-handle drop/highlighting) and `tests/components/mention-query.test.ts` (caret-based autocomplete). `tests/services/comment-service.test.ts` has 2 mention-related cases (resolves `@admin`, emits `comment.created` with resolved mentions). There is **no test for the viewer-exclusion rule** in `resolveMentions`, and no test exercising >100 members or the mismatch between `mentions.ts`'s `handleOf` and `mention-query.ts`'s `mentionHandle` fallback behavior.

## 2. Workspace membership / roles

**Schema**: `src/server/db/schema/members.ts` — `members` table: `id, orgId, userId, role (owner|admin|member|viewer, default member), status (active|invited|suspended, default active), invitedBy, joinedAt, lastSeenAt` + timestamps + soft-delete; unique `(orgId, userId)`. Separate `invitations` table (email, role, tokenHash, expiresAt, acceptedAt, revokedAt).

**Types**: `src/types/member.ts` — `Role = "owner"|"admin"|"member"|"viewer"`, `ROLE_RANK` (owner 4 > admin 3 > member 2 > viewer 1), `hasRoleAtLeast()` (87-89). `MemberStatus = "active"|"invited"|"suspended"`. `Member`, `MemberWithUser` (member + joined `User`), `Actor` (userId/orgId/role/isPlatformStaff) — the principal threaded through every service call.

**Permissions**: `src/lib/permissions.ts` — `ROLE_MATRIX` (25-55) is the single source of truth for minimum role per action (e.g. `"comment:create": "member"`, `"comment:update": "member"`, `"comment:delete": "admin"`, `"comment:read": "viewer"`, `"member:read": "viewer"`, `"notification:manage": "viewer"`). `OWNERSHIP_ESCALATIONS` (58-64) lets the comment's own author update/delete it, and lets a notification's own recipient manage it, regardless of rank. `can()`/`explain()`/`assertCan()` are the only sanctioned entry points (comment at 9-22 says "Nothing else may branch on `actor.role` directly").

**Repository**: `src/server/repositories/member-repository.ts` — `findMember`, `findMemberById`, `listMembers` (filterable by role/status/query), `countActiveMembers` (seat counting), `insertMember`, `updateMemberRole`, `archiveMember` (soft delete, also flips `status` to `"suspended"`, line 169), `touchLastSeen`. `liveMemberPredicate()` (24-26) always filters `archivedAt IS NULL`.

**Service**: `src/server/services/member-service.ts` — `listMembers`, `updateMemberRole()` (40-75: enforces "nobody may grant a role above their own" via `hasRoleAtLeast(actor.role, input.role)`, line 53, plus `assertLastOwnerRetained`), `removeMember()` (81-105, soft delete + last-owner check), `resolveActor()` (112-120: the only place an `Actor` is minted — requires `member.status === "active"`), `assertLastOwnerRetained()` (127-150, scans up to `OWNER_SCAN_LIMIT = 100` owners — same 100-row scan-limit pattern as mentions).

## 3. Notifications / alerts

**Schema**: `src/server/db/schema/notifications.ts` — `notifications` table: `id, orgId, recipientId, kind (NOTIFICATION_KINDS enum), title, body, href, actorId, readAt, channels (JSON array, default `["in_app"]`)` + timestamps. `notificationPreferences` table: `orgId, userId, kind, inApp (bool, default true), email (bool, default true), digestOnly (bool, default false)`, unique `(orgId, userId, kind)`.

**Types**: `src/types/notification.ts` — `NotificationKind`, `NotificationChannel = "in_app"|"email"|"webhook"`, `Notification`, `NotificationPreference`, `DigestEntry`/`DigestBundle` (daily digest).

**Service — the fan-out hub**: `src/server/services/notification-service.ts`:
- `notify(orgId, kind, recipients, payload)` (46-89): for each distinct recipient (deduped via `Set`), **skips the actor themselves** (line 66: `if (recipientId === payload.actorId) continue;`), looks up that recipient's `NotificationPreference` for `kind`, resolves channels via `resolveChannels`, and skips entirely if no channels remain (line 74). Writes one row per surviving recipient via `notificationRepo.insertNotifications`.
- `resolveChannels(preference, flags)` (156-171): `null` preference → `DEFAULT_CHANNELS = ["in_app", "email"]` (line 39/160). Otherwise: `in_app` iff `preference.inApp`; `email` iff `preference.email && (!preference.digestOnly || isEnabled("digest_email", flags))` — i.e. `digestOnly` suppresses immediate email unless the org's `digest_email` plan flag is on, in which case email is *still* sent immediately (the digest flag paradoxically re-enables immediate email rather than deferring it — worth re-reading if "digest" semantics are in scope).

## 4. Issue comments: creation, editing, deletion, threading, count

**Schema**: `src/server/db/schema/comments.ts` — `comments` table: `id, orgId, issueId, authorId, body, parentId (nullable, self-referential for replies), editedAt (nullable), mentionedUserIds (JSON array, denormalised "for the mention fan-out", default `"[]"`)` + timestamps + soft-delete (`archivedAt`). Indexes on `(orgId, issueId)` and `(orgId, archivedAt)`.

**Types**: `src/types/comment.ts` — `Comment` (extends `Timestamps, TenantScoped, SoftDeletable`), `CommentWithAuthor` (+ joined `User`), `CommentThreadNode { comment: CommentWithAuthor; replies: readonly CommentWithAuthor[] }` (one level of nesting only), `CommentDraft`.

**Schema (Zod)**: `src/schemas/comment.ts` — `createCommentSchema` (body 1-10,000 chars, `parentId` nullable default null, `mentionedUserIds` ≤50 default `[]`), `updateCommentSchema` (body only, 1-10,000), `deleteCommentSchema`, `listCommentsSchema` (+ pagination, `includeArchived` default false).

**Service**: `src/server/services/comment-service.ts`:
- `EDIT_WINDOW_MS = 15 * 60 * 1000` (line 31) — **the 15-minute edit limit**.
- `createComment()` (45-85): org-scope assert → load issue → `assertCan(comment:create)` → `assertNotArchived` on the issue → **`consumeRateLimit(orgId, "comment:create")`** (line 59) throwing `Error("Comment rate limit reached; try again after …")` → resolve mentions → insert → `emit("comment.created", { actorEnvelope, commentId, issueId, mentionedUserIds })`.

This means each edit resets/extends the 15-minute window. Non-author editors with sufficient role (e.g. admin, though `comment:update` matrix role is `member` so this mostly matters for ownership escalation nuance) are **not** subject to the time window at all (only checked when `authorId === actor.userId`).

Everything still passes. All fixes are in place:

- **Mentions beyond 100 members**: `member-repository.ts` now has `listAllActiveMembers` (unpaginated), used by `comment-service.ts` instead of the capped 100-row page.
- **Read-only members never mentioned**: removed the `role === "viewer"` exclusion in `mentions.ts`.
- **Shared handle only mentions one member**: `resolveMentions` now maps each handle to every member holding it.
- **Double alert for mentioned assignee/author**: `notification-service.ts`'s `comment.created` handler now drops mentioned users from the "comment added" watcher set so a mention alert takes precedence.
- **Reply-to-reply missing from thread / vanishing under a deleted comment**: `comment-repository.ts`'s `listThread` now walks the full ancestor chain so every descendant (at any depth) stays anchored under its top-level comment, and no longer drops archived comments from the tree; `comment-thread.tsx` no longer filters archived nodes out, letting the existing "This comment was deleted" placeholder render in place.
- **Edit window resets on each edit**: `isPastEditWindow` now measures from `comment.createdAt` instead of `updatedAt`.
- **Editing to add a mention doesn't alert/search doesn't find new text**: `updateComment` now recomputes mentions, persists them, emits a new `comment.updated` event that notifies only newly-mentioned users and re-indexes the comment for search.
- **Flood of comments blocks everyone**: `consumeRateLimit` now accepts a `scope`, and both the action and service layers key the comment-posting bucket per-member (`actor.userId`) instead of per-org.
- **No alert for a reply to your comment**: the parent comment's author is now included among `comment.created` watchers.
- Also excluded the comment author's own handle from recorded mentions, matching the spec.

Typecheck and the full test suite (616 tests) pass.
